revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Puzzle Problem
revealWordProblem.text:
The percentage of each type of puzzle in a toy store before a sale is shown. During the sale, the store sold all of its 300-piece and 500-piece puzzles — 120 puzzles in all.
Question: How many of each type of puzzle did the store have before the sale?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A picture graph of puzzle stock by type: 300-piece 40%, 500-piece 35%, 750-piece 15%, and 1,000-piece 10%.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The puzzles that sold were the 300-piece and 500-piece stock together: 40% + 35% = 75% of the whole stock. So 120 is 75% of the total: 0.75t = 120, giving t = 160 puzzles before the sale. Now take each percent of 160 — 300-piece: 40% of 160 = 64; 500-piece: 35% of 160 = 56; 750-piece: 15% of 160 = 24; 1,000-piece: 10% of 160 = 16. Check: 64 + 56 = 120 sold, and 64 + 56 + 24 + 16 = 160.

conceptIntro.heading: Determine the Whole Given the Part and Percent
conceptIntro.intro: Before you fill in the table, make sure the percent matches the part you know.

conceptIntro.keyIdea: Put the part with the percent that matches it, then scale to 100%. The whole is bigger than the part only when the percent is less than 100%.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Pon la parte con el porcentaje que le corresponde y luego cambia la escala a 100%. El entero es mayor que la parte solo cuando el porcentaje es menor que 100%.

onLevel.stem: A toy store's puzzle stock was 25% 300-piece, 15% 500-piece, and the rest 1,000-piece. During a sale the store sold ALL of its 300-piece and 500-piece puzzles — 120 puzzles in total. How many of each type did the store have before the sale? Explain your reasoning.
onLevel.sampleAnswer: The 120 puzzles sold were the 300-piece and 500-piece stock together, so they represent 25% + 15% = 40% of the whole stock. That makes 120 the part and 40% the percent, with the total stock unknown: 0.4t = 120, so t = 120 ÷ 0.4 = 300 puzzles in all. Now find each type as a part of that whole: 300-piece = 0.25 × 300 = 75 puzzles, 500-piece = 0.15 × 300 = 45 puzzles, and 1,000-piece = the remaining 60% = 0.6 × 300 = 180 puzzles. Check: 75 + 45 = 120 sold ✓, and 75 + 45 + 180 = 300 ✓.
hints: What percent of the stock did the 120 sold puzzles make up?

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake when finding the whole is multiplying by the percent instead of dividing. For "$42 is 60% of the original price," computing 0.6 × 42 = $25.20 makes the original price SMALLER than the sale price — impossible for a discount. Since percent × whole = part, the whole is found by dividing: 42 ÷ 0.6 = $70. Whenever the percent is less than 100%, the whole must come out larger than the part, so a smaller answer is the tell.
